## What's new

- **Reassign index** (DT1 editor). Select one or more tiles and click **Reassign index…** to give them new numbers. A grid shows each selected tile with its **main index**, **sub index** and **kind** (orientation).
  - **Checks on every number.** A tile's frame turns **red** when a DT1 loaded with this one (the map's other libraries, or those of a level type that lists it) has the same number and the tile's rarity is 0, so the game may draw that other tile instead. It turns **orange** when another DT1 has the number: one loaded with it while this tile has a rarity, or any DT1 in the game or your mod. Hover a tile to see which DT1s. Tiles here that share a number (random variants) are noted too.
  - **Quick numbering.** "free" picks the lowest sub index nothing loaded with the DT1 uses. With several tiles, set one main index for all and number the sub indices counting up.
  - **Reassign placed tiles in map** (on by default) shows how many cells of the open map use the old numbers. When you save the DT1, those cells move to the new numbers as one undo step. If you overwrote the DT1, the same Undo puts the DT1 back too. A number that one of its variants keeps stays where it is, and the menu tells you so.
  - **Rules a map can follow:** main index 0–63 and sub index 0–255. Floors stay floors and shadows stay shadows. Walls can become another wall kind. The two halves of a north corner keep their kind and move together.
